solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excellent stages for players of a certain sort?

parts.note: excellent means fine
legs are stages of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Outstanding theatres for a particular kind of performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'players' are cricketers, not actors: FINE LEG is a fielding position behind the batter on the leg side, and the plural names the fielders who stand there.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket fielders posted at that position behind the batsman are named after it, so they are players of one particular sort.

clue.text: A good way towards empty shelters close to Etna

indicators.note: one piece shelters, that is houses, the other
emptied of its middle, so the inner letter goes

parts.note: for can mean towards, as in heading for home

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Quite a distance toward hollow shelters near the volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR with its middle removed is FR, which shelters A, the last letter of 'Etna'.
explanation.definitionFit: Far means a long distance away.

clue.text: Some casinos we attended without difficulties

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: We went to several gambling houses and it was easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something done with no trouble or effort at all.

clue.text: Place one ultimately gets trashed?

parts.note: trashed is slang for very drunk, so the place is the neighbourhood pub where a drinker ends up

explanation.surface: Somewhere that will eventually be vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashed' suggests wrecked; it means drunk. The answer is British slang for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Your nearest regular pub is a classic drinking spot.

clue.text: Cosy up to in-demand reporter?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: cosy means snug
hot means popular, in demand

explanation.surface: Flattering a sought-after journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cosy up to' reads as flatter; 'up' turns SNUG. A 'reporter' here is something that makes a report, a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm's discharge makes a report, a sharp explosive noise.

clue.text: Refusal to go to America shows sense

parts.note: a refusal is a no
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Declining a trip to the States is the sensible choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is informal British for common sense or practical intelligence.

clue.text: Theologian filling in old dance card

indicators.note: the theologian letters fill the gap inside the other pieces

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar completing an old-fashioned dance card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is not the dance card: it is old slang for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing eccentric, as an oddball is a strange person.

clue.text: Ten ailments unfortunately making you tender

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Having lots of illnesses makes one soft-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender and sentimental both describe soft, emotional feelings.

clue.text: God's causing grief on making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the word for causing grief is read from right to left

parts.note: something sore causes pain or grief

explanation.surface: A deity is upsetting people by returning to the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'God' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay, and 'on' is a link too.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: Debating Tory minister, royal loses head

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
to minister to someone is to tend them

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the royal word goes

parts.note: a king is a royal

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician arguing with a beheaded royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun in a political surface but is the verb 'tend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Contending is arguing or asserting a position, as in a debate.

clue.text: Try to follow English actor's case in hearing

indicators.note: the attempt comes after the other pieces
a case is the outside, so the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
a try or attempt is a shot

explanation.surface: Attempting to keep up with a British performer's lawsuit in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' and 'hearing' suggest a court; 'in' is a link and 'in hearing' means within range.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the range of hearing, as in within earshot.

clue.text: Breakfast time item broadcast in parts on radio

indicators.note: said on the radio, so we hear a word sounding like the one meant

parts.note: a serial is a programme broadcast in instalments

explanation.surface: A breakfast programme serialised on the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and similar grains in a bowl are the classic morning meal.

clue.text: Pest men rant about, getting stings

indicators.note: about means around and here signals the letters going round into a new order

explanation.surface: Annoyed men complain about being stung by insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Police stings are entrapments, operations luring someone into crime.

clue.text: Severe singer admitting alto's very busy

indicators.note: letting something in, so the alto letter goes inside the pair of words before it

parts.note: severe means hard
a tit is a small songbird, a singer
A is the abbreviation for alto in music

explanation.surface: A stern vocalist lets in a contralto who is rushed off her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'alto' is 'is', a link. 'Singer' is a crossword favourite for a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard at it means working energetically without a break.

clue.text: Minor country tune Seattle Essentially Bites

indicators.note: to tune is to adjust, so the city's letters are set in a new order
the essence of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A song about Seattle that really bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tune' rearranges SEATTLE into STATELE; 'Essentially' takes the middle letter of 'Bites', T.
explanation.definitionFit: A statelet is a small state, a tiny sovereign territory.

clue.text: Record-breaking English paper like The Guardian?

indicators.note: the two letters break into the record word

parts.note: a list is a record
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A British newspaper smashes records, like the Guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is a British newspaper with left-of-centre politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-wing in outlook, as that left-leaning newspaper is reputed to be.

clue.text: Liberal dons loathed getting arrested

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the loathed word wraps itself round the Liberal letter

parts.note: loathed means hated

explanation.surface: A progressive academic is hated and taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal dons' looks like left-leaning university teachers; 'dons' is the verb, the letter L being worn by HATED. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested in the sense of stopped: an arrested process is one brought to a standstill.

clue.text: Drop of malt and dope provided for rock group?

indicators.note: a drop of something is a small first taste, here the opening letter of the drink

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
provided means if

explanation.surface: A dram of whisky with drugs supplied for a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock group' suggests musicians; it means a mass of rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a geological block of rock.

clue.text: Flipping rare uranium, hydrogen and another element

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: R can stand for rare
U is the symbol for uranium
H is the symbol for hydrogen
plus means and

explanation.surface: Turning over rare uranium and hydrogen with another chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: R, U, H and PLUS are joined then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur is a chemical element, like uranium and hydrogen.

clue.text: Suggest a bit of tomfoolery stops eventually

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so the letters plug into the phrase for eventually

parts.note: in time means eventually

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Hinting that the clowning will end at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: A and T (from 'a bit of tomfoolery') go inside IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to hint or indicate indirectly.

clue.text: Revolutionary soldier of high rank in base

indicators.note: revolving means turned round, so the soldier is reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a noble is of high rank

explanation.surface: A revolutionary aristocratic soldier stationed at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' suggests a camp; it means low and dishonourable. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and ignoble both mean dishonourable or mean-spirited.

clue.text: Resort opening after tough time downsizing

indicators.note: the opening comes after the cut-down piece
cutting down means the last letter goes

parts.note: a mare is British slang for a nightmare experience
a gate is an opening

explanation.surface: A resort opening after a hard period of cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGATE is a seaside resort in Kent. 'Having a mare' is British slang for a terrible time; MARE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is an English seaside holiday town.

clue.text: Menus given new look with oil paint

indicators.note: having a new look means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restaurant menus redesigned with an oily glaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins MENUS to OIL as one pool of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a water-based household paint for walls.

clue.text: Overly-fancy white trousers papa left

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the white word takes the two letters into itself

parts.note: white suggests pure, unsullied
P is papa in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Fancy white trousers left behind by father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like garments but is the verb 'pockets'.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple prose is florid, over-elaborate writing.

clue.text: Gun part

explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a piece in slang, and a fragment of a whole is a piece.

clue.text: Where one finds dinner's up for discussion

definitions.meaning: a meal is served on a surface in the dining room
a proposal still open to debate is laid there

explanation.surface: Dinner is now ready to be talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the meal's place on furniture, and figuratively a matter put forward for negotiation.

clue.text: After regular outages, author gets power on

indicators.note: regular outages mean every other letter is lost, keeping alternate ones

parts.note: P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: After a series of blackouts, the writer has the electricity back.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A, T, O from 'author' and adding P. 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of something.

clue.text: Vintage metal sheds heading for gardens

indicators.note: shedding means losing, so the letter is removed

parts.note: gold is a metal

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Antique metal garden sheds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheds' looks like garden huts; it means loses, and G goes from GOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage means old, from an earlier era.

clue.text: One bound to land on returning in empty skiff

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
emptied of its inside, so just the first and last letters of the boat
coming back means the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone tied to the shore heads back in an empty boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' is not a leap but tied; RE for 'on' (concerning) is a crossword staple, and 'returning' turns it before it goes into the emptied boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer legally tied to the estate he worked.

clue.text: Religious type in Denver upset about Queen

indicators.note: the jumbled city goes round the royal letters
upset means knocked over, so the city's letters are jumbled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A churchman in Colorado is upset about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the city, which then goes round the royal cipher; 'in' is only a link and Denver is not the location of the churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title of a clergyman, and informally a minister himself.
